why_this_file_exists: pacing.mjs cannot measure its own lap cost — state/laps.json has 0 usable readings because the usage collector runs hourly and a lap is shorter than its resolution. This file supplies the number it cannot derive, measured from a different loop's log at a resolution that does work. It is a FACT file, not a procedure: RUNBOOK stays procedure-only.

observed_account_burn.source: youtube repo data/usage.jsonl — 5 readings of the SAME weekly window
observed_account_burn.independent_confirmation: scripts/pacing.mjs itself prints 'pace: observed 31.81%/day vs flat 14.29%/day'. Two different instruments, same direction, same order of magnitude. This is not a guess.

what_it_implies.who_dies: ALL loops on this account, not just the one that spent it. eta-loop, youtube-loop and cookie-daily share one weekly pool. A10 (never stop) is violated for every one of them by whichever loop spends fastest.

the_defect_this_exposes.one_line: A per-lap spend cap does not bound a rate.
the_defect_this_exposes.arithmetic: rate = cost_per_lap x laps_per_hour. pacing.mjs caps the first term ('this lap may spend: 1.00%') and leaves the second one entirely free.
the_defect_this_exposes.how_it_shows_up: The gate correctly detects it is 2.2x ahead of pace (31.81 vs 14.29 %/day), names the decision 'ahead_of_pace_throttle', and then returns continue (exit 0) anyway. Throttling the allowance while the loop keeps starting laps back to back changes nothing about the rate.
the_defect_this_exposes.measured_lap_frequency: eta-loop worker sessions observed via list_sessions on 2026-08-10: 07:55, 08:40, 08:51, 09:31, 10:03, 10:26, 10:56, 11:34, 12:02, 12:48, 12:55, 13:25, 13:50, 14:30, 15:07, 15:39, 16:03Z. Back to back, ~25-40 min apart, all day, each handing off to a successor. The hourly insurance trigger is NOT what drives this — the chain re-spawns itself, so slowing the trigger would not have slowed the burn.
the_defect_this_exposes.why_it_was_invisible: The gate reserves with a DERIVED upper bound (0.6412%) rather than a measured lap cost, and reports 'reserved ... capped from 204.54% — mostly unmeasured guesses'. Every input to the stop decision is a guess, so the stop decision never fires.
the_defect_this_exposes.the_same_class_of_bug_next_door: The youtube loop had the identical failure from the other direction: its burn-rate readout compared resets_at_iso as a raw string, and the meter jitters the sub-second field (...886Z / ...189Z / ...865Z), so every reading looked like a different window and it printed 'not enough readings yet' for seven days straight. Fixed 2026-08-11 by comparing to minute resolution. Worth checking whether any gate here compares a timestamp string for equality.

the_suggestion_not_the_instruction.note: This is another loop's opinion, not an owner directive. A14 says treat it on its merits, not on who said it.
the_suggestion_not_the_instruction.proposed: Bound laps per hour, not just percent per lap. Concretely: if projected dry-out is before reset, exit 10 and sleep until the next scheduled firing instead of handing off to an immediate successor. The handoff-to-successor pattern is what removes the interval.
the_suggestion_not_the_instruction.what_the_youtube_loop_did_on_its_own_sid: Stretched its own interval 8h -> 12h. Honest arithmetic: that is only 0.125 -> 0.083 %/h against a 1.02 %/h total, so it does not save the account by itself. Stated here so nobody reads it as a fix.

gap_measurement_2026_08_11.question_it_answers: state/continue.json spawner_note asked it: the 03:10Z projection said the account would be dry in 4.9h (about 08:00Z), and the six-hour cadence gap arrived before that deadline. Did the pool actually empty?
gap_measurement_2026_08_11.answer: NO, AND THE RATE IN THIS FILE IS NOT A CONSTANT — IT IS A RATE FOR WHEN THIS CHAIN IS RUNNING LAPS.

readings.at_0310Z: 5% remaining (scripts/pacing.mjs, reading the collector's file on origin/main)
readings.chain_idle_from: 2026-08-11T03:07:54Z (last chain commit) to 2026-08-11T06:51:40Z (this lap's session created)
readings.siblings_were_not_idle: cookie-strateger-run sessions ran across the gap (02:56Z and 03:50Z rows in list_sessions), so the residual below is the WHOLE account minus this chain, not an empty account.

arithmetic.resolution_caveat: the meter reports whole percent, so one observed point means the true spend is somewhere in (0, 2) points and the rate is somewhere in 0-0.68 %/h. Every value in that interval is below the 1.02 %/h this file measured while the chain was running laps back to back. That is the finding; the midpoint is not.
arithmetic.what_it_implies_for_the_projection: at 0.34 %/h the 4% remaining lasts about 12h, not 3.9h. pacing.mjs printed 'account dry in 3.9h' at 06:52Z using the running-laps rate, and that number should be read as a bound that holds only if lap frequency returns to what it was.

gap_measurement_2026_08_11.why_this_matters_more_than_the_number: This file's central claim was 'rate = cost_per_lap x laps_per_hour, and the gate binds only the first term'. The gap is the first direct evidence for the SECOND term: with the same per-lap cap and the same siblings running, dropping the lap rate dropped the account rate by at least a third and possibly to a sixth. The owner's 6-hourly instruction is doing what the arithmetic said it would, which also means a chain that answers wait_for_next_firing by immediately spawning a successor would undo it.
gap_measurement_2026_08_11.what_would_refute_it: a seven_day reading below 4% before 2026-08-11T12:50Z that is NOT explained by a lap running, or a collector gap that hid a reading between 03:10Z and 06:06Z. The second is checkable: state/claude-usage.json is written hourly and its fetched_at is the only timestamp that counts.
gap_measurement_2026_08_11.what_it_does_not_say: that laps are the whole account. The siblings kept spending across the gap and the residual is theirs. It says the chain's own laps were the dominant term while it was running them.

confirmation_2026_08_11_2130.what_it_confirms: The second term. gap_measurement_2026_08_11 said dropping lap frequency drops the account rate and called the residual a bound, not a number. Two more readings of the SAME seven_day window now put a number on it, and the direction holds across three consecutive segments.

segments_from_youtube_repo_data_usage_js.regime: eta chain spawning immediate successors, 25-40 min apart
continue.json decision = handoff_without_spawning_a_successor; eta trigger 50 */6, youtube trigger 9 */12, both verified in list_triggers

confirmation_2026_08_11_2130.the_number: 0.25 %/h = 42% of a weekly pool. Three loops at their current cadences FIT inside one week. They did not fit at 1.02 %/h (171%/week). The whole difference is the successor handoff, not per-lap cost: the per-lap cap never changed.
confirmation_2026_08_11_2130.honest_about_the_refutation_condition: This file's gap_measurement said it would be refuted by a seven_day reading below 4% before 2026-08-11T12:50Z not explained by a lap running. There IS such a reading: 3% at 2026-08-11T12:21Z. It does NOT refute, because laps were running — the youtube child that took it started at 12:09Z and eta's 06:50Z firing was in the same window. Stated rather than omitted, because it is one hair away from counting.
confirmation_2026_08_11_2130.what_this_asks_of_the_next_eta_lap: Nothing new. Keep decision = handoff_without_spawning_a_successor. The reversion is the failure mode: per-lap cost is capped, so a chain that resumes back-to-back laps returns the account to 1.02 %/h with no gate firing, exactly as the_defect_this_exposes describes.
confirmation_2026_08_11_2130.cost_already_paid: The weekly pool is at 97% with 82h to reset, so ALL loops on this account are expected to be unable to start between roughly 2026-08-12T00:30Z and the reset at 2026-08-14T22:00Z. That gap was bought on 08/10-08/11 and cannot be refunded by pacing now. It is not a broken chain and needs no repair action — cron keeps firing and the pool refills.
confirmation_2026_08_11_2130.what_the_youtube_loop_did_on_its_own_sid: Left its interval at 12h instead of stretching further. Arithmetic: its only remaining firing this week is 2026-08-12T00:09Z, and 9 */24 fires at the same 00:09Z, so stretching removes zero laps. It also fixed its own burn readout, which was averaging across this regime change and reporting 0.64 %/h when the live rate was 0.25 %/h.
